paper_id: Chen et al. - 2011 - Localization in non-localizable sensor and ad-hoc networks A Localizability-aided approach
title: Localization in Non-localizable Sensor and Ad-hoc Networks: A Localizability-aided Approach
motivation: 实际网络中节点并非全部可定位，既往方法把可定位和不可定位节点同等对待，造成大量无意义的调整和成本
problem_framing: 如何区分可定位与不可定位节点，对网络进行细粒度调整以实现定位
key_insight: 先测试节点局部可定位性，再针对性地通过顶点增强添加必要的边，避免对已是可定位的节点做无谓调整
method_signature: LAL三阶段：局部可定位性测试→组件树构造→网络调整，单轮调整使网络可定位
evaluation_criteria: 与传统IND方法比较添加的边数、组件规模，验证调整的有效性和经济性
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: We consider the method is coarse-grained, since it equally treats localizable and non-localizable nodes
evidence_for_taste: we consider the method is coarse-grained
Ignoring localizability induces a mass of meaningless adjustments
LAL triggers a single round adjustment
adjustments made by LAL are purposefully selected
avoiding meaningless ranging and communication costs
thinking_moves: 先证理论充分条件(RR3P)，再设计工程方案
将粗粒度全局调整细分为组件级别的差异化操作
通过反例(非局部可定位)来揭示既往方法的浪费本质
把定位问题重新框定为可定位性感知的后处理问题
